title: Grandmother first
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in paediatrics. Ollie, 6, was brought in by his grandmother with thirst and weight loss, and tests show he has type 1 diabetes. His parents are driving to the hospital and will arrive in an hour.

His grandmother asks you to tell her the results first, so she can "break it to them gently".
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 4 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Ask her to wait outside until the parents arrive.
options.brief: Dismissive of someone who has been caring for him.
options.detailed: This is correct about the results but excludes her unkindly. It ranks third.

options.text: Offer to talk to her with his parents, if they agree.
options.brief: Includes her, with the parents' consent.
options.detailed: She may be an important source of support. Inviting her, with their agreement, respects everyone. It ranks second because it depends on the parents' wishes.

options.text: Explain kindly that his parents should hear first.
options.brief: His parents have the right to hear about their child's diagnosis first.
options.detailed: His parents have parental responsibility, and the diagnosis is theirs to hear first. Explaining kindly respects the grandmother's good intentions. It ranks first.

options.text: Tell her the diagnosis now, as she brought him in.
options.brief: Shares information without the parents' consent.
options.detailed: Even with good intentions, she doesn't have parental responsibility. Telling her first takes away the parents' right to hear it themselves. It is the least appropriate option.

explanation.issue: This tests how you handle a well-meaning relative's request for information that belongs first to a child's parents.
explanation.keyDetails: His grandmother brought him in. His parents are an hour away. She wants to break the news herself.
explanation.reasoning: [C] declines kindly, and [B] includes her with consent. [A] is correct but unkind, and [D] shares information without consent.
explanation.competing: Some would see telling her as reasonable, as Ollie needs urgent care either way. His treatment can start now, but the diagnosis should be discussed with his parents first.

references.title: 0–18 years: guidance for all doctors
references.note: Sharing information with those with parental responsibility.

references.title: Confidentiality: good practice in handling patient information
